quote.translation: Kant's so-called "lawfulness of the contingent" (Gesetzlichkeit des Zufälligen), that is, the concept of purposiveness (Kant, Kritik der Urteils- kraft, § 76), is likewise nothing other than the necessary-contingent character possessed by a part determined by the whole.

regions.text: なほカントは偶然性を經驗偶然性（empirischeZufalligkcif）〜可想前偶然性（intelligibeleZufalligkeit）～の二種に分けてるるが、カントのいふ経驗的偶然とは我我のいふ羅驗的必然に當の、カントのいふ可想偶然とは我々のいふ形而上的偶然に醤つてるる。

quote.translation: Kant divides contingency into two kinds, empirical contingency (empirische Zufälligkeit) and intelligible contingency (intelligibele Zufälligkeit), and what Kant calls empirical contingency corresponds to what we call empirical necessity, whilst what he calls intelligible contingency corresponds to what we call metaphysical contingency.

regions.text: 「経験的偶然に開してカットは次のやうに云つてゐる。『世界に於ける諸々の變化から經験偶然性すなはち化は継験に限定する原因に依存することが推論されて、経驗的諸制約の上昇系列が得られた』（税料理性批州wse）。

quote.translation: Of "empirical contingency" Kant says: "From the various changes in the world, empirical contingency, that is, the dependence of change on empirically determining causes, was inferred, and an ascending series of empirical conditions was obtained" (Critique of Pure Reason B. 486).

regions.text: また「存在において制約されたものは一般に偶然と雑し、制約されないものは必然と稱す』（BB安）とか「我々は偶然性を或る事象が或る原因の結果としてのみ存在し能ふといふことから認識する。それ故に或るものが偶然的と想定せらるれば、それが或る原因をもつといふのは一つの分析命題である』（Ib,B201）なをと云つてあるのも経驗的偶然に開してである。

quote.translation: It is also of empirical contingency that he speaks when he says that "what is conditioned in existence in general is called contingent, and what is unconditioned is called necessary" (Ib., B. 447), or that "we know contingency from the fact that some event can exist only as the effect of some cause; if something is therefore assumed to be contingent, that it has some cause is an analytic proposition" (Ib., B. 291).

quote.translation: "Intelligible contingency" Kant also calls "contingency according to concepts of the pure understanding" (Zufälligkeit nach Begriffen des reinen Verstandes), and of this kind of contingency he says that "what is contingent in the pure sense of the category is that whose contradictory opposite is possible".
